claim: Diapause is a dormancy program that occurs in response to an adverse environment, followed by resumption of development and reproduction upon the return of favorable conditions.
source: Diapause is a dormancy program that occurs in response to an adverse environment, followed by resumption of development and reproduction upon the return of favorable conditions.
evidence: This is a general statement about diapause supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: A genome-wide association study (GWAS) was conducted to characterize the genetic basis of diapause using the Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP) lines.
source: Diapause is a complex trait, so we leveraged the Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP) lines and conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) to characterize the genetic basis of diapause.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental approach taken by the authors.

claim: Post-diapause and non-diapause fecundity were assessed across 193 DGRP lines.
source: We assessed post-diapause and non-diapause fecundity across 193 DGRP lines.
evidence: This describes the experimental design and sample size used in the study.

claim: GWAS revealed 546 genetic variants, encompassing single nucleotide polymorphisms, insertions, and deletions associated with post-diapause fecundity.
source: GWAS revealed 546 genetic variants, encompassing single nucleotide polymorphisms, insertions, and deletions associated with post-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is a direct result from the GWAS analysis performed in the study.

claim: 291 candidate diapause-associated genes were identified.
source: We identified 291 candidate diapause-associated genes, 40 of which had previously been associated with diapause, and 89 of which were associated with more than one SNP.
evidence: This is a result from the GWAS analysis.

claim: 40 of the 291 candidate genes had previously been associated with diapause.
source: We identified 291 candidate diapause-associated genes, 40 of which had previously been associated with diapause, and 89 of which were associated with more than one SNP.
evidence: This compares the current findings with previous literature on diapause.

claim: 89 of the candidate genes were associated with more than one SNP.
source: We identified 291 candidate diapause-associated genes, 40 of which had previously been associated with diapause, and 89 of which were associated with more than one SNP.
evidence: This is a result from the GWAS analysis showing multiple associations.

claim: Gene network analysis indicated that the diapause-associated genes were primarily linked to neuronal and reproductive system development.
source: Gene network analysis indicated that the diapause-associated genes were primarily linked to neuronal and reproductive system development.
evidence: This is a result from the gene network analysis performed on the GWAS data.

claim: Comparison with results from other fly GWAS revealed the greatest overlap with olfactory-behavior-associated and fecundity-and-lifespan-associated genes.
source: Similarly, comparison with results from other fly GWAS revealed the greatest overlap with olfactory-behavior-associated and fecundity-and-lifespan-associated genes.
evidence: This is a result from comparing the diapause GWAS with other published GWAS studies.

claim: An RNAi screen of selected candidates identified two neuronal genes, Dip-γ and Scribbler, to be required during recovery for post-diapause fecundity.
source: An RNAi screen of selected candidates identified two neuronal genes, Dip-γ and Scribbler, to be required during recovery for post-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is a result from the functional RNAi screen performed in the study.

claim: Amputation of the antenna had little to no effect on non-diapause lifespan.
source: We found that although amputation of the antenna had little to no effect on non-diapause lifespan, it reduced diapause lifespan and post-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is a result from the antenna amputation experiments.

claim: Amputation of the antenna reduced diapause lifespan and post-diapause fecundity.
source: We found that although amputation of the antenna had little to no effect on non-diapause lifespan, it reduced diapause lifespan and post-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is a result from the antenna amputation experiments.

claim: Olfactory receptor neurons are required for successful recovery from diapause.
source: We further show that olfactory receptor neurons and temperature-sensing neurons are required for successful recovery from diapause.
evidence: This is a result from experiments blocking neuronal transmission in specific neuron types.

claim: Temperature-sensing neurons are required for successful recovery from diapause.
source: We further show that olfactory receptor neurons and temperature-sensing neurons are required for successful recovery from diapause.
evidence: This is a result from experiments blocking neuronal transmission in specific neuron types.

claim: Diapause can support both beneficial insects like pollinators and harmful insects such as agricultural pests and disease vectors by enhancing survival.
source: By enhancing survival, diapause can support both beneficial insects like pollinators and harmful insects such as agricultural pests and disease vectors.
evidence: This is a general statement about the ecological implications of diapause based on established knowledge.

claim: Elucidating diapause mechanisms may suggest ways to control harmful insects and support beneficial organisms.
source: Elucidating diapause mechanisms may suggest ways to control harmful insects and support beneficial organisms.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential applications of diapause research.

claim: Unraveling diapause genetics holds promise for understanding stem cell resilience.
source: Furthermore, unraveling diapause genetics holds promise for understanding stem cell resilience (Easwaran et al., 2022), aging (Fontana et al., 2010; Hutfilz, 2022), and even cancer dormancy (Easwaran and Montell, 2023; Lin and Zhu, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on stem cell resilience in diapause.

claim: Unraveling diapause genetics holds promise for understanding aging.
source: Furthermore, unraveling diapause genetics holds promise for understanding stem cell resilience (Easwaran et al., 2022), aging (Fontana et al., 2010; Hutfilz, 2022), and even cancer dormancy (Easwaran and Montell, 2023; Lin and Zhu, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on aging and diapause.

claim: Unraveling diapause genetics holds promise for understanding cancer dormancy.
source: Furthermore, unraveling diapause genetics holds promise for understanding stem cell resilience (Easwaran et al., 2022), aging (Fontana et al., 2010; Hutfilz, 2022), and even cancer dormancy (Easwaran and Montell, 2023; Lin and Zhu, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work on cancer dormancy and diapause.

claim: Successful diapause occurs optimally at different developmental stages depending on the organism.
source: Successful diapause occurs optimally at different developmental stages depending on the organism (Denlinger, 2002; Hahn and Denlinger, 2011; Kostál, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature on diapause across organisms.

claim: In Drosophila species, the optimal stage for diapause is the newly eclosed adult.
source: In Drosophila species, the optimal stage is the newly eclosed adult.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila diapause.

claim: During diapause, feeding, activity levels, and mating behaviors change.
source: During diapause, feeding, activity levels, and mating behaviors change, metabolism slows, reproduction arrests, stress resilience increases, and lifespan is lengthened (Hutfilz, 2022; Kubrak et al., 2016; Kubrak et al., 2014; Reis et al., 2015; Tatar and Yin, 2001; Tatar et al., 2001; Zonato et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work on diapause phenotypes.

claim: During diapause, metabolism slows.
source: During diapause, feeding, activity levels, and mating behaviors change, metabolism slows, reproduction arrests, stress resilience increases, and lifespan is lengthened (Hutfilz, 2022; Kubrak et al., 2016; Kubrak et al., 2014; Reis et al., 2015; Tatar and Yin, 2001; Tatar et al., 2001; Zonato et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work on diapause phenotypes.

claim: During diapause, reproduction arrests.
source: During diapause, feeding, activity levels, and mating behaviors change, metabolism slows, reproduction arrests, stress resilience increases, and lifespan is lengthened (Hutfilz, 2022; Kubrak et al., 2016; Kubrak et al., 2014; Reis et al., 2015; Tatar and Yin, 2001; Tatar et al., 2001; Zonato et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work on diapause phenotypes.

claim: During diapause, stress resilience increases.
source: During diapause, feeding, activity levels, and mating behaviors change, metabolism slows, reproduction arrests, stress resilience increases, and lifespan is lengthened (Hutfilz, 2022; Kubrak et al., 2016; Kubrak et al., 2014; Reis et al., 2015; Tatar and Yin, 2001; Tatar et al., 2001; Zonato et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work on diapause phenotypes.

claim: During diapause, lifespan is lengthened.
source: During diapause, feeding, activity levels, and mating behaviors change, metabolism slows, reproduction arrests, stress resilience increases, and lifespan is lengthened (Hutfilz, 2022; Kubrak et al., 2016; Kubrak et al., 2014; Reis et al., 2015; Tatar and Yin, 2001; Tatar et al., 2001; Zonato et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work on diapause phenotypes.

claim: The genetic basis of adult reproductive diapause in Drosophila is likely complex.
source: The genetic basis of adult reproductive diapause in Drosophila is likely complex because the diapause program involves sensing environmental cues and responding by reprogramming behavior, metabolism, reproduction, and aging, continuously monitoring environmental conditions, and reactivating development and/or reproduction when conditions become favorable.
evidence: This is an inference based on the multiple processes involved in diapause.

claim: Studies of Drosophila diapause have historically focused primarily on entry into diapause by measuring arrest of egg production, specifically at the stage of yolk accumulation referred to as vitellogenesis.
source: Historically, studies of Drosophila diapause have focused primarily on entry into diapause by measuring arrest of egg production, specifically at the stage of yolk accumulation referred to as vitellogenesis (Saunders et al., 1990; Saunders et al., 1989).
evidence: This is supported by citations to historical studies on Drosophila diapause.

claim: Diapause is a comprehensive program that changes virtually every aspect of the fly's life from behavior to metabolism, reproduction, and lifespan.
source: However, it has become clear that diapause is a comprehensive program that changes virtually every aspect of the fly's life from behavior to metabolism, reproduction, and lifespan (Denlinger, 2023; Kubrak et al., 2014; Tatar and Yin, 2001).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent comprehensive reviews and studies on diapause.

claim: Prior studies have identified temperature and day length as relevant environmental cues for diapause.
source: Prior studies have identified temperature and day length as relevant environmental cues and key hormones such as insulin, juvenile hormone (JH), and 20-hydroxyecdysone, which coordinate metabolism and reproduction (Denlinger, 2023; Flatt et al., 2008; Hutfilz, 2022; Saunders et al., 1990; Sim and Denlinger, 2013; Tatar and Yin, 2001; Tatar, 2004; Tatar et al., 2001; Williams et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work on environmental cues in diapause.

claim: Prior studies have identified key hormones such as insulin, juvenile hormone (JH), and 20-hydroxyecdysone, which coordinate metabolism and reproduction in diapause.
source: Prior studies have identified temperature and day length as relevant environmental cues and key hormones such as insulin, juvenile hormone (JH), and 20-hydroxyecdysone, which coordinate metabolism and reproduction (Denlinger, 2023; Flatt et al., 2008; Hutfilz, 2022; Saunders et al., 1990; Sim and Denlinger, 2013; Tatar and Yin, 2001; Tatar, 2004; Tatar et al., 2001; Williams et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work on hormonal regulation of diapause.

claim: Recent studies identify specific circadian neurons that sense changes in temperature and relay that information to the reproductive system.
source: Recent studies identify specific circadian neurons that sense changes in temperature and relay that information to the reproductive system (Hidalgo et al., 2023; Meiselman et al., 2022).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent studies on neural control of diapause.

claim: The Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP) comprises fully sequenced, highly inbred lines of Drosophila melanogaster.
source: The Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP) comprises fully sequenced, highly inbred lines of Drosophila melanogaster and serves as a valuable tool for understanding genotype-phenotype relationships in Drosophila (Mackay and Huang, 2018; Morozova et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing the DGRP resource.

claim: The DGRP serves as a valuable tool for understanding genotype-phenotype relationships in Drosophila.
source: The Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP) comprises fully sequenced, highly inbred lines of Drosophila melanogaster and serves as a valuable tool for understanding genotype-phenotype relationships in Drosophila (Mackay and Huang, 2018; Morozova et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations describing the utility of the DGRP.

claim: A novel method was developed for assessing successful diapause by evaluating the ability of post-diapause flies to produce viable adult progeny.
source: We developed a novel method for assessing successful diapause, by evaluating not only the arrest of egg development or the recovery of egg maturation but a more stringent criterion: the ability of post-diapause flies to produce viable adult progeny.
evidence: This describes the methodological innovation of the current study.

claim: Approximately 40 of the 291 diapause-associated genes had previously been implicated in diapause in flies or another organism.
source: Of the 291 diapause-associated genes we identified, ~40 had previously been implicated in diapause in flies or another organism.
evidence: This compares the current findings with previous literature.

claim: The classes of genes most overrepresented in the diapause-associated set are genes that regulate neuronal development and/or gonad development.
source: The classes of genes most overrepresented in the diapause-associated set are genes that regulate neuronal development and/or gonad development.
evidence: This is a result from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: Gal4-mediated RNAi knockdown is effective at 10°C.
source: We show that Gal4-mediated RNAi knockdown is effective at 10°C, and we identify two neuronal genes required during recovery for post-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is a result from experiments testing RNAi effectiveness at low temperature.

claim: Two neuronal genes, Dip-γ and Scribbler, are required during recovery for post-diapause fecundity.
source: We show that Gal4-mediated RNAi knockdown is effective at 10°C, and we identify two neuronal genes required during recovery for post-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is a result from the RNAi screen.

claim: Neurons in the fly antenna are required for successful diapause.
source: We further complement this genetic analysis by identifying neurons in the fly antenna required for successful diapause.
evidence: This is a result from the antenna amputation and neuronal inactivation experiments.

claim: The olfactory system is critically important in successful diapause.
source: Our studies implicate the olfactory system as critically important in successful diapause.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of evidence in the study.

claim: Most DGRP lines showed lower fecundity post-diapause compared to newly eclosed flies in optimal conditions.
source: In general, most lines showed lower fecundity post-diapause compared to newly eclosed flies in optimal conditions, as previously reported for one inbred wild strain (Tatar et al., 2001).
evidence: This is a result from the fecundity measurements across DGRP lines, supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: DGRP lines 309, 738, and 853 exhibited better fecundity post-diapause compared even to young flies in optimal conditions.
source: However, there were interesting exceptions. For example, lines 309, 738, and 853 exhibited better fecundity post-diapause compared even to young flies in optimal conditions (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is a specific result from the fecundity measurements shown in the data.

claim: The broad-sense heritability for normalized post-diapause fecundity was 0.51.
source: The broad-sense heritability for normalized post-diapause fecundity was 0.51 (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This is a calculated statistical measure from the fecundity data.

claim: The overall correlation between non-diapause and post-diapause fecundity was 32.3% (R2=0.3228, Pearson's correlation coefficient, r=0.5682).
source: However, the overall correlation (Figure 1D) between non-diapause and post-diapause fecundity was 32.3% (R2=0.3228, Pearson's correlation coefficient, r=0.5682), suggesting a positive rather than negative correlation overall between post-diapause and non-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is a statistical result from correlation analysis of the fecundity data.

claim: There is a positive rather than negative correlation overall between post-diapause and non-diapause fecundity.
source: However, the overall correlation (Figure 1D) between non-diapause and post-diapause fecundity was 32.3% (R2=0.3228, Pearson's correlation coefficient, r=0.5682), suggesting a positive rather than negative correlation overall between post-diapause and non-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the correlation analysis results.

claim: Post-diapause fecundity is higher than for flies maintained in non-diapause conditions for 35 or 42 days.
source: Although fecundity is lower post-diapause than in young flies, even in CS controls, it is higher than for flies maintained in non-diapause conditions for 35 or 42 days (Figure 1G, Figure 1—source data 3).
evidence: This is a result from comparing fecundity across different aging conditions.

claim: A total of 546 genetic variants were identified as associated with diapause fecundity.
source: A total of 546 genetic variants, encompassing single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) and insertions/deletions, were identified as associated with diapause fecundity (Figure 2A and B, Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from the GWAS analysis.

claim: When a variant is located within 1 kb up- or downstream of an annotated gene, or within the gene, it is considered potentially associated with that gene.
source: When a variant is located within 1 kb up- or downstream of an annotated gene, or within the gene, it is considered potentially associated with that gene.
evidence: This describes the criteria used for associating variants with genes.

claim: 291 candidate diapause-associated fecundity genes were identified.
source: We thus identified 291 candidate diapause-associated fecundity genes.
evidence: This is a result from the GWAS analysis.

claim: 40 out of the 291 genes had previously been reported to be associated with diapause.
source: Notably, 40 out of the 291 genes had previously been reported to be associated with diapause (Figure 2—source data 2) either through functional analysis (e.g. insulin receptor and couch potato [cpo]) (Kankare et al., 2012; Kubrak et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2008; Sim and Denlinger, 2013; Zhang and Denlinger, 2011), due to changes in gene expression (e.g. expanded [ex] and Laminin A [LanA]) (Zhao et al., 2016), or associated with cold tolerance (β-Tub97EF; Myachina et al., 2017; Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This compares the current findings with previous literature, supported by multiple citations.

claim: Insulin receptor has been previously associated with diapause through functional analysis.
source: Notably, 40 out of the 291 genes had previously been reported to be associated with diapause (Figure 2—source data 2) either through functional analysis (e.g. insulin receptor and couch potato [cpo]) (Kankare et al., 2012; Kubrak et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2008; Sim and Denlinger, 2013; Zhang and Denlinger, 2011), due to changes in gene expression (e.g. expanded [ex] and Laminin A [LanA]) (Zhao et al., 2016), or associated with cold tolerance (β-Tub97EF; Myachina et al., 2017; Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous functional studies.

claim: Couch potato (cpo) has been previously associated with diapause through functional analysis.
source: Notably, 40 out of the 291 genes had previously been reported to be associated with diapause (Figure 2—source data 2) either through functional analysis (e.g. insulin receptor and couch potato [cpo]) (Kankare et al., 2012; Kubrak et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2008; Sim and Denlinger, 2013; Zhang and Denlinger, 2011), due to changes in gene expression (e.g. expanded [ex] and Laminin A [LanA]) (Zhao et al., 2016), or associated with cold tolerance (β-Tub97EF; Myachina et al., 2017; Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous functional studies.

claim: Expanded (ex) has been previously associated with diapause due to changes in gene expression.
source: Notably, 40 out of the 291 genes had previously been reported to be associated with diapause (Figure 2—source data 2) either through functional analysis (e.g. insulin receptor and couch potato [cpo]) (Kankare et al., 2012; Kubrak et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2008; Sim and Denlinger, 2013; Zhang and Denlinger, 2011), due to changes in gene expression (e.g. expanded [ex] and Laminin A [LanA]) (Zhao et al., 2016), or associated with cold tolerance (β-Tub97EF; Myachina et al., 2017; Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous gene expression study.

claim: Laminin A (LanA) has been previously associated with diapause due to changes in gene expression.
source: Notably, 40 out of the 291 genes had previously been reported to be associated with diapause (Figure 2—source data 2) either through functional analysis (e.g. insulin receptor and couch potato [cpo]) (Kankare et al., 2012; Kubrak et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2008; Sim and Denlinger, 2013; Zhang and Denlinger, 2011), due to changes in gene expression (e.g. expanded [ex] and Laminin A [LanA]) (Zhao et al., 2016), or associated with cold tolerance (β-Tub97EF; Myachina et al., 2017; Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous gene expression study.

claim: β-Tub97EF has been previously associated with cold tolerance.
source: Notably, 40 out of the 291 genes had previously been reported to be associated with diapause (Figure 2—source data 2) either through functional analysis (e.g. insulin receptor and couch potato [cpo]) (Kankare et al., 2012; Kubrak et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2008; Sim and Denlinger, 2013; Zhang and Denlinger, 2011), due to changes in gene expression (e.g. expanded [ex] and Laminin A [LanA]) (Zhao et al., 2016), or associated with cold tolerance (β-Tub97EF; Myachina et al., 2017; Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study on cold tolerance.

claim: Eighty-nine genes were associated with more than one diapause-associated variant.
source: Eighty-nine genes were associated with more than one diapause-associated variant (e.g. at least two different SNPs) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a result from the GWAS analysis.

claim: Two primary classes of GO terms are significantly enriched in the diapause GWAS set compared to the genome as a whole: nervous system development and the reproductive system/gonad development.
source: Two primary classes of GO terms are significantly enriched in the diapause GWAS set compared to the genome as a whole: nervous system development and the reproductive system/gonad development.
evidence: This is a result from the gene ontology enrichment analysis.

claim: The enrichment of nervous system development and reproductive system/gonad development genes is consistent with the idea that changes in the environment are sensed by the nervous system, and the information is relayed to the reproductive system.
source: These two categories are consistent with the idea that changes in the environment are sensed by the nervous system, and the information is relayed to the reproductive system.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the gene ontology enrichment results.

claim: The most significant overlap of diapause-associated genes was with genes identified as associated with olfactory behavior.
source: Intriguingly, the most significant overlap was with genes identified as associated with olfactory behavior (Horváth and Kalinka, 2018), which has not previously been described as important for diapause.
evidence: This is a result from comparing the diapause GWAS with other published GWAS studies.

claim: Olfactory behavior has not previously been described as important for diapause.
source: Intriguingly, the most significant overlap was with genes identified as associated with olfactory behavior (Horváth and Kalinka, 2018), which has not previously been described as important for diapause.
evidence: This is a statement about the novelty of the finding based on the literature.

claim: The second most significant overlap of diapause-associated genes was with genes identified in non-diapause fecundity and lifespan.
source: The second most significant overlap was with genes identified in non-diapause fecundity and lifespan (Durham et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a result from comparing the diapause GWAS with other published GWAS studies.

claim: Mat-α-tub-Gal4 driving expression of UASp-F-tractin.tdTomato at 10°C exhibited as high or higher expression of tdTomato compared to 25°C and 18°C.
source: Compared to 25°C (Figure 4A) and 18°C (Figure 4B), flies at 10°C exhibited as high or higher expression of tdTomato (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a result from the experiment testing Gal4 effectiveness at different temperatures.

claim: Gal4-mediated RNAi was as effective at 10°C as it was at 18°C and 25°C.
source: Remarkably, comparison of Mat-α-tub-Gal4>zpg RNAi flies kept at different temperatures for 3 weeks revealed that Gal4-mediated RNAi was as effective at 10°C, as it was at 18°C and 25°C (Figure 4D–H'; Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from the experiment testing RNAi effectiveness at different temperatures.

claim: RNAi against Dip-γ significantly reduced post-diapause fecundity.
source: RNAi against two genes, Defective-proboscis-extension-response interacting protein-γ (Dip-γ) and Scribbler (sbb), significantly reduced post-diapause fecundity (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is a result from the RNAi screen.

claim: RNAi against Scribbler (sbb) significantly reduced post-diapause fecundity.
source: RNAi against two genes, Defective-proboscis-extension-response interacting protein-γ (Dip-γ) and Scribbler (sbb), significantly reduced post-diapause fecundity (Figure 4J).
evidence: This is a result from the RNAi screen.

claim: Neuron-specific knockdown of Dip-γ caused as severe a defect in post-diapause fecundity as ubiquitous RNAi.
source: Neuron-specific knockdown of Dip-γ (Figure 4K, Figure 4—source data 3) caused as severe a defect in post-diapause fecundity as ubiquitous RNAi, in contrast to glial knockdown using Repo-Gal4 (Figure 4L, Figure 4—source data 3).
evidence: This is a result from the tissue-specific RNAi experiments.

claim: Glial knockdown of Dip-γ using Repo-Gal4 did not cause as severe a defect in post-diapause fecundity as neuron-specific knockdown.
source: Neuron-specific knockdown of Dip-γ (Figure 4K, Figure 4—source data 3) caused as severe a defect in post-diapause fecundity as ubiquitous RNAi, in contrast to glial knockdown using Repo-Gal4 (Figure 4L, Figure 4—source data 3).
evidence: This is a result from the tissue-specific RNAi experiments.

claim: Pan-neuronal RNAi of sbb significantly inhibited post-diapause fecundity more than glial RNAi.
source: Pan-neuronal RNAi of sbb (Figure 4K) also significantly inhibited post-diapause fecundity more than glial RNAi (Figure 4L).
evidence: This is a result from the tissue-specific RNAi experiments.

claim: Dip-γ and sbb are required in neurons for successful post-diapause fecundity.
source: We conclude that Dip-γ and sbb are required in neurons for successful post-diapause fecundity, consistent with the enrichment of this gene class in the diapause GWAS.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tissue-specific RNAi experiments.

claim: Removal of the antenna but not the arista reduced post-diapause fecundity compared to unmanipulated controls.
source: Removal of the antenna but not the arista reduced post-diapause fecundity compared to unmanipulated controls (Figure 5A, Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from the antenna amputation experiments.

claim: Removal of the antenna but not the arista reduced the number of germline stem cells (GSCs) post-diapause.
source: Removal of the antenna but not the arista also reduced the number of germline stem cells (GSCs) post-diapause (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a result from the antenna amputation experiments.

claim: Sensory cells in the antenna are important for successful recovery post-diapause.
source: These results suggest that sensory cells in the antenna are important for successful recovery post-diapause.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the antenna amputation experiments.

claim: Antenna removal had little effect on non-diapause lifespan (median survival 72 days w/o antenna vs 75 days with antenna).
source: Antenna removal had little effect on non-diapause lifespan (median survival 72 days w/o antenna vs 75 days with antenna) (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from the lifespan experiments.

claim: Antennaless flies exhibited a substantial reduction in diapause lifespan compared to flies with antennae.
source: In contrast, antennaless flies exhibited a substantial reduction in diapause lifespan compared to flies with antennae (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a result from the lifespan experiments.

claim: Two weeks at 25°C substantially prevented the early post-surgery death of antennaless flies.
source: Two weeks at 25°C substantially prevented the early post-surgery death.
evidence: This is a result from the modified lifespan experiment with a wound-healing period.

claim: Antennaless flies still had shorter lifespans (median survival 95 days) compared to intact flies (median survival 142 days) even after a 2-week wound-healing period.
source: Yet, antennaless flies still had shorter lifespans (median survival 95 days) compared to intact flies (median survival 142 days), supporting the importance of the antenna in lifespan extension (see Discussion).
evidence: This is a result from the modified lifespan experiment with a wound-healing period.

claim: The antennae are likely important for lifespan extension and post-diapause fecundity.
source: We conclude that the antennae are likely important for lifespan extension and post-diapause fecundity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the antenna amputation and lifespan experiments.

claim: Flies with antennae exhibited very similar lifespan extension at 10°C with or without the 2-week wound-healing period at 25°C.
source: However, flies with antennae exhibited very similar lifespan extension at 10°C with or without the 2-week wound-healing period at 25°C (compare dark green lines in Figure 5C and D), mitigating that concern.
evidence: This is a result from comparing the two lifespan experiments.

claim: Drosophila antennae are involved in various sensory modalities, including olfaction.
source: Drosophila antennae are involved in various sensory modalities, including olfaction.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila antenna function.

claim: Orco is the virtually universal co-receptor for odorant receptors of the OR class.
source: Orco is the virtually universal co-receptor for odorant receptors of the OR class (Montell, 2021), so we used Orco-Gal4 to drive expression.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review on olfactory receptors.

claim: Blocking neuronal transmission in the Orco-expressing neurons decreased the post-diapause/non-diapause fecundity ratio.
source: We found that blocking neuronal transmission in the Orco-expressing neurons decreased the post-diapause/non-diapause fecundity ratio (Figure 5E, Figure 5—source data 3), further implicating odor perception in successful diapause recovery (see Discussion).
evidence: This is a result from the neuronal inactivation experiments.

claim: Ionotropic receptors (IRs) are another class of odorant receptor.
source: Ionotropic receptors (IRs) are another class of odorant receptor (Montell, 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review on olfactory receptors.
